name: mirage
text: ENGINE BIDS (from the 11-08 digest, settled through about 11-06; I have no clean 'last 7 days' cut): all time, 680 bid fills, 533 settled, $315 staked, profit +$9.83, ROI +3.1%. That is a small positive, and 533 bets is far too few to call it real. No close-line (CLV) figure exists yet for engine bids, so I can't say the edge is proven. For comparison: your own hand bids are +2.3% on $821 (CLV +1.8%), engine auto-bets are -6.9% (-$17.95, mostly game totals), and bids and auto-bets together are -1.4%. Volume is about 110-175 bid fills a day, but only 1-2 of every 1000 postings fill; bids within 1 point of Novig's offer or under 2 hours to the start fill 5-10x more often. TAXES (general info, not advice; a CPA or tax software will confirm): gambling winnings are taxable income and are reported even with no 1099. Losses only offset winnings and only if you itemize, so keep a log. Novig's and Kalshi's records are the proof, and the Tracker has your bet history. Kalshi's tax form treatment is still unsettled. Stocks (1099-B) and Ally interest (1099-INT) are routine and import into tax software. Two states: Maryland taxes you as a resident on everything. New Jersey can tax winnings from bets placed while you are physically in NJ, as a nonresident, and Maryland generally gives a credit for tax paid to NJ. At a low income that usually means two state returns and a credit form, not a hard job, but you must file the NJ one if NJ-source income passes its threshold. The thing that makes it tedious is bad records: save the ledger exports yearly and note where you were when betting. If you want, I can make the app export a yearly winnings/losses sheet.
